    time, each engine's tests and reference rooms holding before and after, the two engines'
    pictures of one room compared. After 264.

   keeping their names and not their milliseconds. Item 208 closes; the parked forms of items 213

    commits "weird", that the shared modules' repositories are right, that the engine's own content
    could be modulated the same way inside its repository, and that a "one process approach", one
    running process edited and seen as it changes, is worth thinking about; at 18:30 they approved
    the review's recommendation. The direction is that each engine stays one repository and becomes
    one solution of many projects, each an area with its own public surface and its own plugin,
    packed as its own package at one version for all, as Bevy's crates are in Bevy's one repository;
    the dependency direction is held by project references and a norm test over them; the flat API
    stays unchanged on top and a game names the packages it needs; the names are dotted .NET names
    and not com.; there is no editor, and the live path is a watcher that recompiles a changed
    shader, reloads a changed asset or scene and recompiles a changed behavior into the running
    process, the engine's own code by restart. It is scheduled after the current items and done as
    one mechanical batch per engine with the public API held identical before and after and the
    documents' tables redrawn. Items 225 and 226, BevyCSharp Decision 85.

Every cascade traces the same count of rays each frame, yet their cost falls fourfold from the
first to the fourth, so a ray's cost is in what it meets and shades near the eye more than in its
count. The coarser cascades, 1 to 3 at 1.5 ms together, trace whole every frame though their
light changes slowest; the far cascade's quarters a frame are the way already in the engine to
spread them. That cut changes what moves, so it waits on ore.turn and is read by the turn and the
rooms.

Item 250, the reads' commands. Ore takes ore.turn, a turn by degrees a frame for a count of
frames, and ore.walk, a step the way the player faces a frame for a count of frames, each column's
top stood on rather than walked, and ore.status gives the eye and the point it looks at in the
invariant culture. Two runs at a fixed frame time read alike to the thousandth: a degree a frame
for 90 frames turned the view from facing -z to +x, and 0.1 a frame for 120 frames went from 24.50
to 36.73, the 0.23 past twelve the step down the columns from 9 to 5, alike in each run.

Item 250, the coarser cascades in halves. The cascades past the first, the far cascade aside, now
trace half their probes a frame while they lie where they lay the frame before and no change of the
lights or the field lies within the 16 frames a change takes to settle, those whose coordinates add
up to the frame's parity, the other half keeping its rays' light of the frame before, and a probe
carried with its rays moving traces every frame for its cycle. Ore at High at 1280 by 720, under the
lock held alone, 600 frames each: 8.53 and 8.54 ms traced whole, 7.90 and 7.91 in halves, 0.63 ms
saved; gi.state sampled 100 times read the coarser cascades in halves in all 100 standing and in 87
of 100 on the autopilot's walk, 12 whole, after sections were built. On a path through the rooms
frame by frame against the whole trace, with a second whole trace as the floor reading 0.000: the
still and a turn the same to the pixel, a walk of four passes along the big room's diagonal at most
0.030 percent of pixels past 6, the cut with 251's lift 0.873 on its second frame. The first form
spread through changes too, and the suite found what the rooms' reads did not: the panel's room in a
render texture at Low kept a tenth of its light ten frames after the panel went dark, 6.1, 5.9, 3.9
down to 0.6 where traced whole it fell to 0 the frame after, the half keeping the light of before
handing it back through the light past the first bounce; and the sun put out over the open court
differed from the whole trace on the frame after by 40.6 percent of pixels past 6 and arrived a
frame later. Waiting for the change to settle, the panel's room falls to 0 the frame after and
every frame after the sun's step reads as the whole trace's, so a change of light costs nothing and
Decision 95 has no cost to record. gi.toggle spread off traces every probe each frame and gi.state
says which cascades trace in halves; docs/global-illumination.md says both. The test settles the
court in halves and whole, finds them alike, puts the sun out, finds the cascades whole through the
settling and in halves after, and every frame after the step alike; spread through the change, its
first frame differs and the test fails, as the panel's test failed in the suite. The saving goes
where a program's lights and field keep still: each change traces the coarser cascades whole for the
16 frames after it, so Ore's walk halved them in 87 of 100 samples, a game stepping its sun every 83
frames traces them whole for 16 of each 83, and one that streams its land as the player moves, a
section built every few frames, halves them little while moving and fully once it stands; a game
reads its own share by gi.state on the package that carries the spread.

Item 250, the faint glow lights at a hit. The read by part of the screen probes' pass, Ore at High
at 1280 by 720 under the lock held alone, found the glow lights' forms at the probes' rays' hits the
largest cost left: with the hits given no glow light the frame went from 7.93 to 4.77 ms, the

7.8 with 0.5 to 1.3. A light giving a hit under a 32nd of the largest of the lights before it now

Item 255, read and the first of its mends. The driver's own cache stands under XDG_CACHE_HOME, so
an empty one is a player's first run: there the voxel game's terrain pipeline took 12,099 ms to
compile without the layer, and with that folder's driver cache warm and the engine's file missing
93 ms. Half of the 12 s is a second copy of litLight in the game's shader, from its line calling lit
on its unlit branch, which can never reach the light: with unlit there the fragment went from
1,303,784 to 702,448 bytes and the cold compile from 12,365 and 13,627 ms to 5,865 and 5,242. That
line is the game's; the shaders guide now says lit and litLight each carry the whole lighting, so a
shader calls one once and unlit on an unlit branch. The cold first frame of shaders_bounce_rooms
from an empty cache folder took 28,594 and 30,102 ms, its 26 pipelines made one after another on
the frame's thread, the probes' nine kernels about 22.5 s of the driver's time, gi_screen 6.1 and
the trace's four builds 3.2 to 6.2. The probes' kernels are now made together on workers at the
first frame that traces them, the frame waiting for all: the first frame 12,322 and 12,148 ms, the
driver's time 30.9 s spread across them. The test draws the Cornell box's first frame with the
kernels made one after another and together, finds one compile in the driver at a time the first
way and two at once the second, a first compile on a worker waiting for a second to reach it, and
the two frames the same.

Item 256, the engine as one package, after the sibling's 77941f42. The areas' projects are not
packable, 3DEngine/Directory.Build.props saying so for all, and the flat project packs. While
packing its project references are private, so the nuspec names no area. A target carries each
project reference's dll and xml from ReferencePath into lib, the 13 areas' and the Sky module's, and
a second carries their pdbs into the symbols package, where each area's own symbols package held
them before. The outside packages the areas build on are named again in the flat project, seven
added (SDL3-CS.Native, Vortice.Vulkan, AssimpNetter, NVorbis, NLayer, BepuPhysics, BepuUtilities),
and N 2.8's test now also holds each to the version every area naming it names; N 2.8's text in
NORM.md is yours to widen to it. The renderer's target that carried Sky is gone, the flat project
carrying it. No area packed natives of its own or checked anything before its nuspec; SDL3's,
cimgui's and assimp's come from outside packages, which the natives' test reads from the one
package's dependencies.

pack.sh packs the one project with its restore and build. A pack with no build after the release
build left the 13 areas as dependencies, since NuGet takes a reference's privacy from the restore
and only the pack's own restore is marked as packing; the build finds the assemblies already built.
Its version check reads 3DEngine.Core.dll inside the one package. build/package-size.py, the
sibling's, says each package against nuget.org's size, and the pack job runs it right after the
pack, before the contents are checked or anything kept or pushed, with PackageSizeTests on a limit of
a few kilobytes, listed under N 1.4 as the other script tests are. The workflows call pack.sh and
packed no area by name, so they keep their steps; the push's glob finds 3DEngine and the templates
alone, so the 13 area ids get no further version. The 21 games' nuget.config files, the 2
templates', BUILDING.md's example, examples-on-package.sh and docs-on-package.py map 3DEngine alone,
and BUILDING.md, DESIGN.md §9 and three project comments say one package. 3DEngine.Templates stays
its own package, its projects naming 3DEngine alone. AGENTS.md's modules row says the package
carries them, which stays true, so AGENTS.md is unchanged.

The local package 6.2.41-local.256, 6,641,343 bytes, 97.47 percent of nuget.org's size left,
against 4,965,314 for 257.1's flat package and 7,011,723 for its fourteen. It holds lib/net10.0 with
the dll and xml of 3DEngine, of the 13 areas and of Sky, 30 entries; analyzers/dotnet/cs with the
generator and its code fixes; README.md, LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and logo.png; 316 content
files, the shaders and their compiled cache; and its nuspec, whose 11 dependencies are the outside
packages and none of the engine's. Its symbols package holds the 15 pdbs. Every example of
3DEngine.Examples, copied outside the repository as examples-on-package.sh copies them, restored
3DEngine 6.2.41-local.256 alone and built with warnings as errors, and no area package of that
version was restored. PackageContentsTests read the package and pass, the areas in its lib and none
a dependency.

The pack run compares no capture by its bytes. compare.py counts a pixel apart past 24 of 255 and
holds each example to the share it recorded within a point, and captures.tsv's hashes are of the
captures kept in .github/assets/examples, so the gallery is made again only when they are taken
and kept again. The sibling draws through its own renderer and its pictures do not move. The game
draws through this engine's composite with a curve of its own choosing and no temporal
antialiasing, so its pictures move by up to a level wherever a channel is neither black nor white,
the grain still from frame to frame, and none of its tests reads a capture's colors.

The suite passed in order, 2,352 in 39 minutes, while the machine carried another session's game
and a load near 10. The shuffled leg then reached its 40 minutes at AppLeakTests' app 77 of 100 with
2,334 passed, which test.py counts as passing, a loss to the time limit alone; 18 tests had not run,
so the shuffled leg alone ran again once the load fell, 2,352 passed in 24 minutes.

1,440 rows, the rows alone setting how a glow texel spans the depth's texels, drawn 88 frames, the

settled from frame to frame. On the GPU the strips hold 31.79 to 31.97 frames and change 0.0017 to
0.0121 levels between the last two; on the head's shader before a64815c7 both cases fail. On
lavapipe here, Mesa's CPU device held to four threads and four cores, the cases took 59 s at Low and
1 min 12 s at High, holding 31.81 to 32.00 frames and changing 0.0009 to 0.0020; drawn 48 frames,
High had changed 0.095 at 1,440 rows there and 0.103 on the GPU, so 80. The ceiling's test took
1 min 23 s and 1 min 39 s on lavapipe at 640 and 480 wide; at 160 and 120 wide, the same rows, it

Item 263, the dither's grain as the owner chose it. build/blue-noise.py writes
3DEngine/Shaders/dither/blue_noise.bin, 64 by 64 texels of rank by Ulichney's void-and-cluster
method with a Gaussian of 1.2 texels and a fixed seed, a byte a texel; at a tenth of the table no
two texels touch, where at 1.5 eight pairs did. The composite loads it once into the 64 slices of a
cube at binding 4 of its set, and frameDither reads a texel by its pixel, still from frame to frame,
moved by the golden ratio each frame only under temporal antialiasing. The dither is on unless
SetDither(false), which leaves the bands, and SetDitherStrength sets its grain from 0 to 1, a half
unless set: at a half even across a level, the owner's fourth picture; at 1 the triangle across
two levels, the third; between, their quantiles blended; under a half even across less than a level,
the bands coming back toward none at 0. GetDitherStrength, the listing, the cheat sheet, the guide's
rows and a slider in the effects' window carry it.

DitherTests' window is 64 rows. On the ramp the default changes 0.431 of neighbors, strength 1
0.562, off 0.063; the means 15.264, 15.263 and 15.271; a column of one light takes 2 levels at a
half and 3 at 1, held so; each four by four block's mean lies 0.0510 and 0.0562 levels from its
column's, against 0.071 for the interleaved gradient's grain in the same bin, the bound 0.065; black
stays black. On lavapipe here, four threads on four cores, its tests take 2 s and 1 s. The eight
tests that read a capture exactly hold again with the default on, their 191 neighbors passing; no
play compares a picture, and compare.py counts a pixel apart past 24 of 255, so none else was
touched. Rounded to whole levels the triangle's blue noise clumps a fifth less than the gradient's
at most levels and alike at a half level, while the even grain keeps the table's spread best,
which is why the owner saw the half the calmest. The owner chose, on four pictures at 2560 by 1440
of the lantern room and sheets of one patch at four times, both blue grains, the strength in code,
the dither on, the grain still, no table over time, and the 10-bit swapchain later.
